result: Id2 gene expression is highly enriched in cortical interneurons that do not express PV, SST, or VIP, and the Id2 interneuron population includes cells expressing markers such as Reelin, NPY, NDNF, Lamp5, and Sncg.
evaluation: Claims C1-C6 are supported by analysis of published scRNAseq data from Tasic et al., 2016 and Yao et al., 2021, as shown in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1. The data demonstrate that Id2 expression is enriched in non-PV/SST/VIP interneurons and co-occurs with known markers of this population.

result: Intersectional genetics using Id2-CreER and Dlx5/6-Flpe drivers with the Ai65 reporter yields labeling of interneurons in all cortical layers, with Id2 interneurons comprising 18% of the overall interneuron population in S1BF and prelimbic cortex, predominantly located in superficial layers (L1-3).
evaluation: Claims C7-C11 are supported by experimental data from intersectional genetic labeling (Figure 1C-F, Figure 1—figure supplement 2) with quantitative cell counting from 4 brains (680/3812 cells = 18%). The distribution and proportion are consistent with previous estimates from Tremblay et al., 2016 and Yao et al., 2021.

result: The vast majority of Id2 interneurons (>95%) are distinct from PV, SST, or VIP populations, and almost all cortical Id2 interneurons originate from non-Nkx2.1 lineages (i.e., from the CGE/POA).
evaluation: Claims C12-C16 are supported by intersectional genetic labeling experiments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3, demonstrating minimal overlap between Id2 and PV/SST/VIP populations. The data show extremely sparse labeling in Id2-CreER; Nkx2.1-Flpo; Ai65 and Id2-CreER; VIP-Flpo; Ai65 crosses, with citations to Valero et al., 2021 for MGE-derived Id2 cells in L6.

result: The majority (87%) of Id2 interneurons in L2-5 are NPY-expressing neurogliaform cells, with layer-specific proportions ranging from 29% in L1 to 95% in L4-5. In L1, about 30% are NPY-expressing NGFCs, with the remainder comprised of canopy cells and α7 cells.
evaluation: Claims C17-C24 are supported by fluorescence in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2A-B, with 638 cells counted from three brains. The layer-specific proportions are clearly documented, and the L1 composition is consistent with previous analysis from Schuman et al., 2019. The inference that Id2/NPY cells are NGFCs is supported by established associations between NPY expression and NGFCs in superficial layers.

result: Overall in L2-6 of S1BF, 15% of Id2 labeled interneurons exhibit strong CCK expression, with Id2/CCK cells most abundant in L2 (14%) and L6 (25%). About 80% of the Id2/non-NPY population in L2/3 are CCK+ interneuron subtypes, such that Id2/NPY and Id2/CCK populations account for nearly all of the Id2 interneurons in L2-5.
evaluation: Claims C25-C29 are supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2C-D, with 165/1123 cells counted from three brains. The lack of overlap between CCK and NPY is consistent with previous work (Kubota and Kawaguchi, 1997) and scRNAseq data (Yao et al., 2021). The inference that Id2/NPY and Id2/CCK account for nearly all Id2 INs in L2-5 is mathematically consistent with the reported proportions.

result: The majority (80-90%) of randomly recorded Id2 cells in L2-5 exhibit a late-spiking firing pattern with electrophysiological and morphological properties typical of neurogliaform cells, including high connection probability (70%) to pyramidal cells and slow IPSC decay kinetics.
evaluation: Claims C30-C37 are supported by electrophysiological recordings from 76 randomly selected Id2 cells (Figure 3, Table 1), paired recordings from 27 cell pairs, and morphological reconstructions from 15 cells (Figure 3A-B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1). The proportions of late-spiking cells match the proportions of Id2/NPY cells from histology, and the properties are consistent with previous descriptions of NGFCs (Tamás et al., 2003; Oláh et al., 2009; Overstreet-Wadiche and McBain, 2015).

result: The remaining Id2 cells (~20% in L2/3 and ~10% in L4-5) exhibit irregular or bursting firing patterns with narrower action potentials, express CCK, exhibit depolarization-induced suppression of inhibition (DSI), and have morphology consistent with CCK basket cells.
evaluation: Claims C38-C49 are supported by electrophysiological recordings (Figure 3C-F, Table 1), histological analysis (Figure 2), DSI experiments (Figure 4), and morphological reconstructions (Figure 3C-D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1). The optogenetic DSI experiments show ~20% suppression of GABA release, consistent with the proportion of non-LS cells. Paired recordings demonstrate DSI in 3/5 connected non-LS-PC pairs but 0/9 LS-PC pairs. The morphology is consistent with published descriptions of CCK basket cells (Galarreta et al., 2004; De May and Ali, 2013).

result: Eleven Id2 interneurons were identified as light-responsive in silicon probe recordings in freely moving animals, exhibiting wide waveform characteristics and wider auto-correlograms. These cells, located primarily in deeper layers (L3-5) where >90% of Id2 cells are NGFCs, are tentatively concluded to be neurogliaform cells.
evaluation: Claims C50-C56 are supported by in vivo silicon probe recording data shown in Figure 5B-E, with stringent filtering criteria applied to identify 11 light-responsive Id2 INs. The waveform characteristics and auto-correlograms distinguish these cells from narrow waveform interneurons. The inference that these are NGFCs is based on the combination of recording location (deeper layers where >90% of Id2 cells are NGFCs based on Figure 2) and waveform properties, though this remains tentative as acknowledged by the authors.

result: Putative Id2 neurogliaform interneurons exhibit relatively consistent firing rates across behavioral conditions with moderately increased activity during REM sleep, and show a robust rebound in activity immediately following cortical down-states during NREM sleep (observed in 64% of cells), which is negatively correlated with down-state suppression and may be mediated by intrinsic membrane properties.
evaluation: Claims C57-C62 are supported by in vivo silicon probe recording data shown in Figure 5F-J. The rebound in activity following down-states is statistically significant (p<10⁻¹⁰, chi-squared test) and observed in 64% of putative Id2 NGFCs versus 7%, 14%, and 1% for PC, NW, and WW interneurons, respectively. The negative correlation between down-state suppression and post-down-state rebound is shown in Figure 5I. The suggestion that intrinsic membrane properties mediate this rebound (C61) is appropriately speculative based on the observed correlation.

result: Light stimulation of Id2 interneurons results in a significant decrease in firing rate for about half of all cell types, with pyramidal cells in supra-granular layers more frequently suppressed than deeper layer pyramidal cells. A slow positive activity modulation of a subset of interneurons and pyramidal cells is also observed, with positively modulated responses lagging negative responses, suggesting an indirect disinhibitory mechanism.
evaluation: Claims C63-C69 are supported by optogenetic stimulation and in vivo recording data shown in Figure 6A-D. The broad inhibition is consistent with the extensive connectivity of NGFCs. The layer-specific differences in suppression and the temporal lag of positive responses relative to negative responses are clearly documented. The inference of an indirect disinhibitory mechanism (C68) is reasonable based on the temporal lag, though alternative explanations are not explicitly ruled out.

result: Background knowledge claims about cortical interneuron origins, lineages, and proportions are accurately cited from the literature.
evaluation: Claims C70-C72, C76-C77, and C87-C92 are supported by appropriate citations to established literature (Xu et al., 2008; Liodis et al., 2007; Lee et al., 2010; Tremblay et al., 2016; Rudy et al., 2011; Vucurovic et al., 2010; Wamsley and Fishell, 2017; Hu et al., 2017; Lim et al., 2018; Gelman et al., 2009; Hu et al., 2014; Riedemann, 2019; Lee et al., 2013; Pi et al., 2013; Keller et al., 2020; Kullander and Topolnik, 2021; Schuman et al., 2019). These claims provide necessary context for the study and are consistent with established knowledge in the field.

result: Background knowledge claims about neurogliaform cell and CCK basket cell properties are accurately cited from the literature, including their connectivity, electrophysiological properties, morphology, and in vivo behavior.
evaluation: Claims C73-C75 and C78-C86 are supported by appropriate citations to established literature (Tamás et al., 2003; Oláh et al., 2007; Oláh et al., 2009; Overstreet-Wadiche and McBain, 2015; Bodor et al., 2005; Galarreta et al., 2008; Tremblay et al., 2016; Schuman et al., 2019; Hestrin and Armstrong, 1996; Wozny and Williams, 2011; Kawaguchi, 1995; Jiang et al., 2013; Jiang et al., 2015; Kubota et al., 2011a; Zhou and Hablitz, 1996; Valero et al., 2021). The inference that CGE-derived NGFCs behave distinctly from MGE-derived NGFCs (C86) is supported by the absence of down-state active cells in Id2 IN recordings (Figure 5G) combined with knowledge that MGE-derived NGFCs are down-state active.
